'''Boris Shraiman''' is an American theoretical physicist working on [[statistical physics]] and [[biology]]. He is a Permanent Member of the [[Kavli Institute for Theoretical Physics]] and the Susan F Gurley Professor of Theoretical Physics and Biology at the [[University of California, Santa Barbara]].<ref name="homepage">{{cite web|url=https://www.kitp.ucsb.edu/shraiman |title=Boris Shraiman &#124; KITP |publisher=Kitp.ucsb.edu |date= |accessdate=2022-05-02}}</ref>

== Biography ==
Shraiman earned a PhD from [[Harvard University|Harvard]] in 1983 and did postdoctoral work at the [[University of Chicago]] in the [[James Franck Institute]]. In his early work, Shraiman addressed how dynamical systems transition to chaos and how patterns form in viscous flows and dendritic growth.<ref>{{cite journal
|title=Scaling Theory for Noisy Period-Doubling Transitions to Chaos
|author1=B. Shraiman |author2=C. E. Wayne |author3=P. C. Martin
|journal=Physical Review Letters
|volume=46
|issue=14
|pages=935–939
|year=1981
|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.46.935
|bibcode=1981PhRvL..46..935S }}
</ref><ref>{{cite journal
  |title = Viscous flows in two dimensions
  |author = D. Bensimon, L. P. Kadanoff, S. Liang |author4=B. I. Shraiman |author5=C. Tang
  |volume = 58
  |issue = 4
  |pages = 977–999
  |year = 1986
  |journal = Reviews of Modern Physics
|doi = 10.1103/RevModPhys.58.977
 |bibcode = 1986RvMP...58..977B |s2cid = 54051923 }}</ref> He moved to [[Bell Labs]], where he worked on quantum materials,<ref>{{cite journal
|title =Spiral phase of a doped quantum antiferromagnet
 | author1=B. I. Shraiman |author2=E. D. Siggia
 |journal = Physical Review Letters
 | volume =62
  |issue = 13
  |pages = 1564–1567
  | year = 1989
  | doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.62.1564 | pmid=10039706 | bibcode=1989PhRvL..62.1564S }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal
|title=Fermi-liquid-to-polaron crossover. II. Double exchange and the physics of colossal magnetoresistance
 |author1 = A. J. Millis | author2=R. Mueller |author3= B. I. Shraiman
 | journal = Physical Review B
 | volume = 54
 | issue = 8
 | pages = 5405–5417
 | year = 1996
 |doi = 10.1103/PhysRevB.54.5405 |pmid = 9986499 |arxiv = cond-mat/9602155 |bibcode = 1996PhRvB..54.5405M |s2cid = 827848 }}</ref> then later became a professor at [[Rutgers University]] in 2002 and the [[University of California, Santa Barbara]] in 2004. He has advanced the understanding of [[turbulent]] fluids,<ref>{{cite journal
|url =https://www.nature.com/articles/35015000
|author1=B. Shraiman |author2=E. Siggia
|title=Scalar turbulence
|journal=Nature
|volume=405
|pages=639–646 
|year=2000
|issue=6787 |doi=10.1038/35015000 |pmid=10864314 |bibcode=2000Natur.405..639S |s2cid=4359554 |url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal
|url=https://www.nature.com/articles/nature05464
|author1=M. Vergassola |author2=E. Villermaux |author3=B. Shraiman
|title='Infotaxis' as a strategy for searching without gradients
|journal=Nature
|volume=445
|pages=406–409 
|year=2007
|issue=7126 |doi=10.1038/nature05464 |pmid=17251974 |bibcode=2007Natur.445..406V |s2cid=8973078 |url-access=subscription}}</ref> and since 2000, his work has built connections between statistical physics and biological problems.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uctv.tv/shows/KITP-Chair-Endowment-Adventures-at-the-Edge-of-Physics-18581|title = VIDEO: KITP Chair Endowment / Adventures at the Edge of Physics}}</ref> In particular, his research has pointed to the interplay between mechanics and [[morphogenesis]], which addresses the problem of "growth and form" in animal development,<ref>{{cite journal 
|title=Mechanical control of growth: ideas, facts and challenges
|author1=K. D. Irvine |author2=B. I. Shraiman

|issue=23

|doi=10.1242/dev.151902
|pmid=29183937

}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal

|pages=3318–3323
|doi=10.1073/pnas.0404782102
|pmid=15728365
|pmc=552900

|doi-access=free
}}</ref> and developed models to describe evolutionary dynamics in populations such as [[influenza]].<ref>{{cite journal

|doi-access=free

He became a member of the National Academy of Sciences in 2011.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/boris-i-shraiman-ikga5j/|title=Boris I. Shraiman}}</ref>
Shraiman chaired the 27th [[Solvay Conference]] in Physics: "Physics of Living Matter: Space, Time and Information" in 2017.  
<ref>{{cite web|url=https://solvayinstitutes.be/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/Proceedings-Physics-2017.pdf|title=Proceedings of the 27th Solvay Conference on Physics - The Physics of Living Matter: Space, Time and Information}}</ref>
